items.title: v2.1.316
items.author: ashwin-ant
items.excerpt: What's changed Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK, which turns the ultrathink keyword off Added pooled group budgets to the Claude apps gateway: one monthly budget that a group's members share, on top of each member's own limit, set with pooled_budget on the spend limits admin API Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_LOOPED_CROSS_CERT_DROP to keep system cross-certificates that certify each other in a loop, for servers whose private CA needs one Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's Added managed.policy_mode: layered to the Claude apps gateway: every policy that matches a developer applies, each merged over the ones listed below it, not only the first Added guardrail.input_tagging on Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, which wraps prompts in the input tags that an Amazon Bedrock guardrail's prompt attacks filter needs; all_messages_and_system also tags the system prompt Deprecated fast mode for Opus 4.8 as of October 30, 2026; it will be removed on November 30, 2026. After removal, fast mode requests on Opus 4.8 return an error and do not fall back to standard Opus 4.8. Migrate to Opus 5.5 to keep the speedup Fixed shell commands being left running on macOS and Linux when Claude Code exits by itself, for example when credentials are refused or a cloud session is archived Fixed bash aliases with line breaks in their value (except in Git Bash), and functions whose names start with a dash, being garbled or lost in the Bash tool's shell Fixed bash scripts started from the Bash tool stopping after their first command when SHELLOPTS is exported Fixed PowerShell hooks not blocking on exit code 2 when the command begins with a type cast, param, using or an attribute Fixed some network requests hanging when a compressed response was cut off or corrupted Fixed sonnet, opus and haiku on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error mid-session instead of switching to an older model
items.why_it_matters: New Claude Code release adding a subagent effort setting, pooled group budgets, an ultrathink disable flag and CA certificate handling. Directly affects daily agentic workflows and team spend controls.

items.title: [AINews] Google admits AI Mode hurts Search revenue; -15% $500B drop worst since 2004 IPO. AI Bear Market coming?
items.author: swyx .ai
items.excerpt: As an engineer-focused newsletter we only very rarely let financial stories through (our last example was Jan 2025), but when this is about the future of Google and Google Search, with a recently departed AI leadership, you cannot not care. At its heart is the tension between overview pages and underlying pages they summarize. Any good enough summary obviates the need for you reading the source. Google’s Featured Snippets or Knowledge Panels have long had that tension with the publishers that supply that data. But now, Google’s own AI Overviews are potentially affecting traffic with… Google's Search revenue. Google doesn’t break out AI Mode in sufficient detail that we can make any sort of rigorous analysis, but most people are quoting Philipp Schindler (Chief Business Officer): “It’s worth noting that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.” Together with other bad earnings results it set off a range of steep declines throughout tech: View post on X ↗ This is against a backdrop of souring tech/AI sentiment in public markets - and with OpenAI raising at $1.25T not $1.4T, not the sort of thing you want in the lead up to one of the biggest tech IPOs of all time. items.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
items.author: Richard MacManus
items.excerpt: At AI Engineer New York this month, we sat down with Aman Singh, the lead AI Engineer at Arca, an “AI-native” company providing wealth management services. We discovered that while agents do most of the background work in the firm, there are guardrails in place to ensure that human advisors are making the final decisions. The goal is for AI to guide the process; or as Singh nicely put it, “agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.” Arca recently raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock. One of the features of using AI in financial services, explained Singh, is that it’s typically long-horizon work — although not long-running. In his AIE presentation, Singh noted that agent tasks at Arca can take up to ten days. “It's very stop-start, there's many actors in between, many decision points, many handoffs,” he said. For this reason, Arca has developed an internal memory system. “So we have this persistence for every client,” Singh said in our podcast discussion. “What has happened so far? What are we tracking for next? What needs to happen immediately in the next couple of days [and] what are we tracking for the long term? Which individual is responsible for which action? All of this is being tracked by our memory systems that our agents contribute to.” Arca uses models from frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, with Claude its primary model provider. The company has built its own harness, which automatically selects the best model to use for a particular task, based on the company’s internal benchmarks. Owning the harness, rather than using a managed agent harness, also means that Arca has the flexibility to change model providers if it needs to. Safety is obviously key for financial services. Singh noted that although agents do much of the work, an agent’s role is limited to analysis and proposing solutions. items.title: datasette-llm 0.1a9
items.excerpt: Release: datasette-llm 0.1a9 I have some big upgrades to Datasette Agent in the pipeline, but in the meantime here's a tiny user experience improvement to the underlying datasette-llm plugin. It now picks up the default model used by LLM, which means you can start using Datasette Agent without needing to explicitly configure a default model: uvx --with datasette-agent datasette content.db --internal internal.db Previously you would also need to specify a model with -s plugins.datasette-agent.default_model gpt-6-astra. Tags: datasette, llm, datasette-agent

items.title: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts
items.excerpt: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe. It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data. Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard, which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe. That message receiving code uses innerHTML, so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method. This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions. OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it. Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference. The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf. OpenAI closed the hole and paid out a $5,000 bug bounty, which I think was a bit cheap for a vulnerability this serious. Via Hacker News Tags: iframes, javascript, sandboxing, security, xss, openai, chatgpt, content-security-policy
items.why_it_matters: Detailed ChatGPT account-takeover chain via a sandboxed HTML preview and a third-party JS library (MathLive). Useful lessons for anyone building artifact or iframe sandboxes in AI products for clients.

items.title: Building ChatGPT for Finance — Joseph Kim, OpenAI's Head of Financial Services
items.author: Latent Space
items.excerpt: What does it take to build AI for finance on top of a general-purpose model? Joseph Kim, who leads work on ChatGPT for Financial Services at OpenAI, joins swyx and Richard at AI Engineer New York to discuss the decisions behind the product: training financial reasoning into a shared model, connecting market data, and building workflows financial professionals can review and trust. Joseph explains why OpenAI bundled financial data even when connectors already existed, what startups can build with the same plugin primitives, and why human taste and expert judgment are hard to measure. The conversation moves from analyst workflows and review chains to investment ideas and the problem of building useful financial evaluations.
